newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebel leader urges civilians against panic.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel leader urges civilians against panic.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila has told residents of the eastern city of Goma to stop panicking over an expected counter-attack by government forces.

"Once again the people of Goma are panicking. It seems people in Kinshasa will counter-attack but why are you running away?" Kabila, chairman of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL), told a news conference in Goma on Tuesday, dispelling rumours he had fled Zaire.

Some 200 residents left Goma after Zaire's Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo on Monday ordered the start of a counter-attack, expected from Kisangani to the northwest. But by Wednesday many people had returned to Goma which the rebels seized in November.

Residents of rebel-held areas have been nervous since President Mobutu Sese Seko returned to Kinshasa last month from cancer treatment in Europe vowing to wrest a swath of eastern Zaire from the AFDL. Mobutu went back to France this month.
"People in (rebel-held) Bunia are not intimidated by the declarations from people in Kinshasa. I would like you to behave like responsible people who have recovered their freedom," Kabila said.

Some 5,000 people fled Amisi village near Mahulu 260 km (160 miles) southeast of Kisangani after reports of clashes between the Rwandan-backed rebels and Rwandan Hutu fighters, the U.N. refugee agency said on Tuesday.

Rebels are ready for a counter-attack on their 600-km (400-mile) -long stretch of territory bordering on Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi which they seized in an offensive that began in October with the stated aim of ousting Mobutu.

But security sources in the region said on Monday that the rebels' military commander, Andre Kisase Ngandu, had been killed in an ambush near the rebel-held town of Butembo, probably by Mai-Mai tribal warriors who were formerly part of the rebel alliance.
Asked about the reports, rebel spokesman Raphael Ngenda said Kisase was wounded and declined all further comment.
Justin Muwelwa, a leading member of the alliance, indicated at a seminar for some 500 youths in Goma on Tuesday that Kisase had been killed but stopped short of confirming it outright.
"If Kisase dies, that is a pity but we are fighting. Do not weep, take your weapon and fight and if the enemy kills one of you kill one, two, three or more," he said.
Seeking to bolster rebel strength, Kabila on Tuesday visited a training base for recruits at Rumamgabo, 40 km (25 miles) north of Goma and told them to be on guard against rumours.
"Show the people you are strong. Do not heed rumours. Denounce anyone who sows seeds of division among you and he will be punished," he told the recruits.
"The FAZ (Zairean army) say they will counter-attack but who will welcome them when they are corrupt, rotten? The first attitude you must have is to respect civilians," Kabila said.
